problem: Two triangles with equal corresponding adjacent sides and equal included angles have equal bases, are congruent, and have equal corresponding remaining angles.
proof_idea: Derive equal included dot products from equal squared side lengths and sign-sensitive angle congruence. Invoke the existing SAS metric law, then recover the remaining angle relations and fold triangle congruence. The library SAS theorem takes dot equality; this bridge must be proved rather than substituted for the source hypothesis.
litex_code:
thm proposition_4:
    ? forall p, q, r, u, v, w cart(R, R):
        $geometry::main::is_triangle(p, q, r)
        $geometry::main::is_triangle(u, v, w)
        $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(p, q, u, v)
        $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(q, r, v, w)
        $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
        =>:
            $geometry::main::are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
            $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(q, p, r, v, u, w)
            $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(p, r, q, u, w, v)
    claim:
        ? forall x, y R:
            x^2 = y^2
            x * y >= 0
            =>:
                x = y
        by contra:
            ? x = y
            x != y
            x - y != 0
            (x - y) * (x + y) = x^2 - y^2 = 0
            x + y = 0 / (x - y) = 0
            y = -x
            x * y = x * (-x) = -(x^2)
            x^2 = -(-(x^2)) = -(x * y) <= 0
            x^2 >= 0
            x^2 = 0
            x = 0
            y = -x = 0
            x = y
            impossible x != y
    release thm geometry_lemmas::triangle_vertices_distinct(p, q, r)
    release thm geometry_lemmas::triangle_vertices_distinct(u, v, w)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(p, q)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(u, v)
    geometry::main::distance_sq(q, p) = geometry::main::distance_sq(p, q) = geometry::main::distance_sq(u, v) = geometry::main::distance_sq(v, u)
    have first R = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(p, q, r)
    have second R = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(u, v, w)
    geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r) > 0
    geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r) $in R+
    have denominator R+ = geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r)
    geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = geometry::main::distance_sq(q, p) * geometry::main::distance_sq(q, r)
    geometry::main::angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = geometry::main::distance_sq(v, u) * geometry::main::distance_sq(v, w) = geometry::main::distance_sq(q, p) * geometry::main::distance_sq(q, r) = geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = denominator
    first^2 * denominator = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(p, q, r)^2 * geometry::main::angle_cos_den(u, v, w) = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(u, v, w)^2 * geometry::main::angle_cos_den(p, q, r) = second^2 * denominator
    first^2 = second^2
    first * second = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(p, q, r) * geometry::main::angle_cos_num(u, v, w) >= 0
    first = second
    geometry::main::dot(geometry::main::vec(q, p), geometry::main::vec(q, r)) = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(p, q, r) = first = second = geometry::main::angle_cos_num(u, v, w) = geometry::main::dot(geometry::main::vec(v, u), geometry::main::vec(v, w))
    release thm geometry::main::sas_congruence(p, q, r, u, v, w)
    p != r
    u != w
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(p, r)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(u, w)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(q, r)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_symmetric(v, w)
    geometry::main::distance_sq(r, p) = geometry::main::distance_sq(p, r) = geometry::main::distance_sq(u, w) = geometry::main::distance_sq(w, u)
    geometry::main::distance_sq(r, q) = geometry::main::distance_sq(q, r) = geometry::main::distance_sq(v, w) = geometry::main::distance_sq(w, v)
    by def $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(r, p, w, u)
    by def $geometry::main::are_triangles_congruent(p, q, r, u, v, w)
    by thm geometry_lemmas::angle_congruence_from_equal_sides_and_dot(p, q, r, u, v, w) => $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(q, p, r, v, u, w)
    by thm geometry_lemmas::angle_congruence_from_equal_sides_and_dot(r, p, q, w, u, v) => $geometry::main::are_angles_congruent(p, r, q, u, w, v)

comments.critical_bridge: Equal included angles with equal adjacent lengths imply equal dot products. Squared-cosine equality alone is insufficient without sign.
